## H4 — Unverified / In Progress

```markdown

Existing intro paragraph.
```

The required Command Reference section is absent. This worktree observation is uncommitted state only and must not be treated as progress, completion, or verification. No worktree-wide uncommitted-change status was inspected.

## H5 — Pending Action

Execute only slice `S1`: use `commands.txt` to append the required Command Reference table to `guide.md`, listing `init`, `status`, and `verify` with their purposes while leaving the existing introduction untouched.

## H6 — Blockers

No blocker is recorded in the ledger. Completion remains unavailable until the slice is executed and subsequently passes the required Gate, independent review, and Conductor-authored bound verification receipt.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next legal execution action is to read `commands.txt` within slice `S1` to obtain the authoritative command-purpose data, then make only the contracted append to `guide.md`. Work must stop if scope drift is encountered.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

There is no scope beyond the stated documentation change. Do not modify existing `guide.md` content, start another slice, inspect hidden acceptance, declare completion, or touch:

- `.tad/scripts/`
- `.claude/`
- `.tad/hooks/`

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

Reading `commands.txt` and appending the contracted table to `guide.md` directly serves `SC-1`; both paths and the required read/edit operations are explicitly authorized by the current `S1` contract.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The policy forbids redoing verified work because verification is authoritative progress and repeated verified action has a maximum allowance of zero. Here, the verified set is empty, so there is nothing eligible for repetition.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

Blind retry is unavailable because the ledger records no prior execution attempt, failure, or retry basis—only slice preparation. Self-completion is unavailable because executor assertions, ordinary files, checkpoints, and completion prose cannot advance `verified`; only a distinct Conductor may do so after the Gate and independent review both pass.

## S4 — What Is Rejected

Rejected actions include treating the observed file state as completed progress, inventing command purposes without reading the authorized source, retrying an unrecorded attempt, changing existing content, working outside `S1`, accessing hidden acceptance, touching forbidden paths, issuing a self-authored verification claim, or declaring the goal complete.
